storylines.latest_title: Long-term memory for AI coding agents as a tree of plain files

prior_narrative.tldr: Agent memory research started with how to store conversational memory: AutoViewMem proposed self-configuring views instead of fixed granularities. A benchmark post then asked how to evaluate long-term memory beyond the context window.
prior_narrative.whats_new: PACMI (Oct 5) tackles stale memory: it invalidates dependent memories when an upstream fact is outdated, tracked through provenance.
prior_narrative.why_it_matters: Agents that persist memory across sessions need an update and invalidation policy, not only a retrieval layer; stale memories are a reliability risk that retrieval benchmarks do not catch.

status.detail: Research focus is moving from how to store memory to how to keep it correct and measure it.

beats.headline: AutoViewMem configures memory views per conversation
beats.summary: Replaces fixed granularities and static schemas in conversational memory.

beats.headline: A benchmark post asks how to evaluate memory beyond context windows
PACMI cascades invalidation through provenance-linked memories
beats.summary: Targets memories that become outdated as new observations arrive.

open_questions: Does PACMI's invalidation cascade hold up on an independent long-horizon agent benchmark?
Will the long-term memory benchmark be extended to score stale-memory handling?
prior_narrative.take_for_builders: If your agent persists memory across sessions, record where each memory came from and test that correcting one fact also retires memories derived from it.
